The test suite is exhaustive and explicitly covers all the required failure domains.\n\n### Findings\n\n**No actionable defects or issues found.** \nThe implementation strictly adheres to the requirements, perfectly balancing security (symlink escaping, `.git` injection, environment isolation) with functionality (legacy flat fixtures vs. paired history).\n\n***\n\n• **Overall Code Quality Summary:** \nThe patch demonstrates senior-level engineering rigor. Embedding standard-library Python within the bash wrapper is an elegant way to achieve robust file and JSON parsing without introducing external dependencies. The isolation of the Git environment (clearing `GIT_*` vars, overriding `hooksPath` and `gpgsign`) ensures reliable offline execution regardless of the caller’s local Git configuration. The accompanying `test-review-eval-staging.sh` leverages `unittest` beautifully, proving the robustness of the changes through extensive positive and negative boundary tests. \n\n• **Top 3 Priority Fixes:** \n- None required. The implementation is remarkably clean and ready for integration.\n\n• **Positive Aspects:** \n- **Git Environment Isolation:** The meticulous clearing of inherited `GIT_*` environment variables and explicit inline config overrides (`core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, `commit.gpgsign=false`) eliminates common automation failure vectors.\n- **Robust Security Checks:** The `validate_tree` function correctly anticipates symlink escaping (including dangling links), directory traversal, and repository pollution (`.git`, `oracle`, `eval.json`).\n- **Seamless Test Integration:** Using `sys.argv.pop()` to extract the dynamically injected repository root before invoking `unittest.main()` is an incredibly clean trick that keeps the test harness self-contained and easy to run.\n- **Backwards Compatibility:** The graceful fallback to staging legacy flat test-files against an empty base commit perfectly preserves existing evaluations without requiring manual migrations.",
